column1: # Who owns a function's instructions, for scripts/bench-owners.sh.
# Columns, tab separated: kind, owner, regular expression (awk ERE). Rules of a kind are tried in
# file order and the first match wins.
#   std   -      a path (`core::`, `alloc::`) that is skipped when looking for the crate a generic
#   raw   owner  the whole demangled symbol; for libc and asm that have no Rust path. Tried first.
#   path  owner  the first path in the symbol that is not `std`, e.g. `podgate::h3::bridge::send`.
#   file  owner  the source file of an instruction line from the line tables (`--by file`). A line
#                that no file rule matches, or has no file, takes the owner of its function; so
#                inlined library code (`core`, `alloc`) stays with the function it was inlined into.
# An owner that no rule names is `other`. The spec's owner list, in the order it names them:
# quinn, h3, podgate h3 (front, endpoint, limits), internal h2 hop, shared pipeline, tls, allocator,
# other. The h1 codec only runs for the HTTPS reference. The kernel is not here: callgrind counts
# guest instructions only, a system call is one instruction (see docs/benchmarks.md).
# Owners that are library code any layer calls. `--inherit` charges them to the owners that call them.
